item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
In the end, this page more or less boils down to this

+
-

SCP-723-J-# is a Periplaneta Americana (American cockroach) believed to be a relative to SCP-723-J.

SCP-723-J-#'s anomaly manifests as a pun.

SCP-723-J-# Intake Log Interview

Dr. ██████: SCP-723-J-#, did you do your thing again?

SCP-723-J-#: [does thing]

Dr. ██████: Oh you

SCP-723-J-#: [does thing again]

Dr. ██████: Isn't this humorous? I'm talking to a cockroach, and it's not talking back! How wacky!

SCP-723-J-#: [Continues to do thing]

Dr. ██████: no.

It worked for fad roach, but overstayed its welcome after that. -1 for the lack of variety in the humor presented in what is ostensibly supposed to be a joke/humorous tale.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Big thanks to Jacob Conwell and taylor_itkin for reading this over in chat, and also all the people who posted in the discussion page for SCP-723-J with suggestions for the rest of the -ad Roach family, and pretty much everyone in chat who joked with me about said -ad Roach family. Thanks to all of that, this page now exists, as does this: http://www.scp-wiki.net/kiryu-labs-roach-wrangling-log

In all honesty, yes, this is silly. I wrote this a few months ago when it occurred to me that there wasn't a lot of stuff on the mainsite explaining how/why joke SCPs exist in-universe (if they do). My headcanon is that in-universe, researchers write those things up for fun, and so each lab/department has their own set of inside jokes because according to my research that's how nerds make friends.

ETA: all images are CC-compliant since I took them with my phone. I saw a couple roaches last summer.

Happy New Year everyone.
